question: Can independent brightness strength and alpha distribution be edited visibly without changing the drawn geometry?
hypothesis: Increasing additive spread makes the dark ground visibly grainier; changing the alpha exponent changes coverage on an isolated layer.

parameter.name: range and exponent, tested separately
parameter.unit: byte offsets or alpha factors; dimensionless exponent

comparison: Native p5 Canvas2D candidate at pixelDensity1, fixed geometry seed42 and independent grain state42. Compare raw pixel differences and inspect each successful render. Alpha changes operate on an isolated transparent layer before composition, not the finished scene.
constraints: one causal parameter changed per comparison
no recommended range inferred from these discrete values
source noise/RNG and rendering differences are declared
all native execution uses the shared machine lease
provenance: survey/out/2014/Generativos/minimalCirculines/variants/grain_20/result.json: none, mean0.0095, fraction0, following blur is a confound
survey/out/2016/Generativos/ThePiper/notes.md: signed jitter4->20 subtle; missing font weakens whole-scene comparison
survey/out/2018/Generativos/quadShadow/notes.md: shader alpha exponent0.4, source evidence only; density warning
decision_rule: Retain the controls if replay is exact, geometry stays unchanged, and inspected output displays their stated mechanism. If the intended effect is absent, diagnose visibility/capture/order before revising the boundary. Keep default and encouraged range null; these observations cannot establish a continuous useful interval.
root_observation: Root inspected all six native states. At high0 the dark ground is flat, high10 fine grain, high40 clearly coarser contrast; block geometry is unchanged. Alpha exponents .4,1,2 progressively reveal more ground within the same layered rectangles. Exact replay/save checked by browser.
conclusion: Retain both explicit controls; no default or continuous recommended range inferred.
